reproduction_manifest.eval_command: rm -f experiments/repro_mnist_imgs/affNIST/*.npy && python3 test_mnist_classification.py --config configs/affnist/logsumexp_diffusion.yaml && python3 fid_score.py --true experiments/repro_mnist_imgs/affNIST/padded_mnist.npy --fake experiments/repro_mnist_imgs/affNIST/resnet18_mnist_classifier_logsumexp_diffusion_canonicalized.npy --model lenet -c 0
reproduction_manifest.notes: Successfully reproduced all three rubric metrics. Accuracy 82.53% matches paper's 82.64±0.11 (within CI [82.53, 82.75]). FID 5.04 matches paper's 5.05. Wall-clock runtime ~37.25 min on A100 matches paper's 37 min on A6000. Minor multiprocessing cleanup error on exit is benign.
reproduction_manifest.eval_output_format: Accuracy: grep 'test accuracy' or final 'average accuracy' from stdout (percentage). FID: parsed from 'FID (...): X.XX' in stdout.
reproduction_manifest.known_levers: steps (diffusion steps, 50 default): increase for more thorough sampling at linear runtime cost. num_mc (MC sample size, 2 default): increase for better score estimation at linear cost. num_hypothesis (ensemble K, 64 default): increase for better hypothesis selection at linear cost. noise_min/noise_max (0.1/1.0 default): tune noise schedule range for exploration-exploitation tradeoff. temperature (1.0 default): adjust Boltzmann temperature. dtype (float32/float64): use float64 for higher precision at higher memory cost.

Dependencies: easydict==1.13, lightning==2.6.1, scipy==1.15.3, matplotlib==3.10.8, bayesian-optimization==3.2.0, kagglehub==0.4.3. optimization_objective.summary: Improve affNIST test accuracy and FID of TIED on ResNet18 under affine transformations Aff(2,R) with classifier logit confidence energy, while minimizing wall-clock runtime. The three metrics are antagonistic: accuracy and FID improve with more compute (diffusion steps, MC samples, ensemble size) at the cost of runtime.

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.rationale: Primary classification performance metric. Paper reports 82.64±0.11. Current reproduction at 82.53. Improvement in accuracy directly demonstrates better transformation inversion quality.

metrics.name: FID
metrics.rationale: Perceptual quality metric measuring distance between inverse-transformed test images and original training distribution. Paper reports 5.05. Lower FID indicates visually better inversion.

metrics.name: Wall-clock Runtime
metrics.rationale: Computational cost measured in minutes on single GPU. Paper reports 37 min on A6000. Any accuracy/FID improvement should not come at disproportionate runtime cost. Pareto dominance rule applies: only accept runtime increase if accompanied by meaningful accuracy gain.

optimization_objective.success_policy: Use Pareto dominance across Accuracy, FID, and Wall-clock Runtime. A solution dominates if it is strictly better on at least one core metric and no worse on any other. Regression tolerance: 0% on Accuracy and FID (no regression allowed), 10% on Runtime (can go up to ~41 min if justified by accuracy/FID gains). Core levers to tune: diffusion steps (accuracy-runtime tradeoff), MC sample size (estimation quality), ensemble size (hypothesis selection quality), and noise schedule bounds.
